default.notes: Visa required — apply at a Surinamese embassy or consulate, or online where your nationality is offered the e-visa. The cheap e-Tourist Card is not available to this nationality.

groups.notes: CARICOM nationals enjoy freedom of movement under the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas — normally admitted for six months on arrival with no tourist card or visa; holders of a CARICOM Skills Certificate may live and work in Suriname.
No visa needed for tourism, but an e-Tourist Card (about USD 25) must be bought online before departure — single entry, up to 90 days. Business visits need a visa instead.
Visa-free for short tourist stays under the bilateral agreement — no tourist card required; confirm the current allowance with a Surinamese mission before a longer trip.

SR.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Surinamese citizens.

NL.notes: Dutch visitors still need the e-Tourist Card despite the historic ties; those holding a Surinamese-origin document (PSA card) are exempt and enter on that instead.

VE.notes: A visa is required in advance; Venezuelan nationals face additional checks at Surinamese borders, so allow extra processing time.
